title: Microsoft Purview DLP: rules to auto-resolve and tag alerts
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned alert-resolution and tagging rules and distinguishes them from existing alert handling. The roadmap dates match, and targeted searches confirm the stated gaps in feature-specific controls, defaults and licensing documentation.

claims.claim: The planned capability belongs to Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention - Rule-based tagging and auto-resolution of alerts based on business needs of the customer.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans rules that resolve predictable alerts the organisation does not need to see.
claims.quote: Resolve alerts you don't need to see - e.g., Low-severity alerts for mail sent only to your trusted partner domains, so they never reach your triage queue.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; front matter: confidence
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this planned feature, whose specific behaviour is known from the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: DLP auto-resolution rules; Purview alert tagging rules; trusted partner domains Business Process. Opened dlp-alerts-get-started, dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started, dlp-alert-investigation-learn and dlp-investigate-alerts-defender; results describe existing alert handling, not this feature.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the admin UI or automation for the planned alert auto-resolution and tagging rules.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview alert tagging auto resolution rule PowerShell Graph API New Set alert policy; DLP auto-resolution rules. Read Set-DlpComplianceRule alert/tag parameters, New-ProtectionAlert search excerpts, Graph Update alert and Purview/Defender DLP procedures; none documents these planned rules.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature's default state is unknown, including whether any rule exists or changes existing behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP rule based tagging auto resolution default permissions retention resolved alerts tags. Read roadmap description and Purview/Defender DLP alert pages; no default or arrival behaviour is stated for the planned rules, distinct from Defender's existing built-in tuning rule.

claims.claim: The conditions supported by the planned rules are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DLP auto-resolution rules; Purview alert tagging rules. Read DLP alert get-started/dashboard pages and policy-reference search excerpts; no condition reference for the planned alert-handling rules was found. Roadmap examples are not a supported-condition specification.

claims.claim: How the planned rule tags are named is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview alert tagging rules; Purview DLP rule based tagging auto resolution default permissions retention resolved alerts tags. Read DLP alert and Defender investigation pages; custom incident tags and Communication Compliance tags do not specify naming for the planned DLP rule tags.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The visibility, searchability and retention of automatically resolved alerts under these planned rules are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DLP resolved search alerts retention; Purview DLP rule based tagging auto resolution default permissions retention resolved alerts tags. Read dlp-alert-investigation-learn and dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started; general retention is stated, but planned-rule resolved-alert handling is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roles that create or edit the planned alert-handling rules are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP rule based tagging auto resolution default permissions retention resolved alerts tags. claims.claim: Prerequisites specific to the planned alert-handling rules are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP alert auto-resolution tagging rules licensing price meter service description; DLP auto-resolution rules. Read DLP alerts/dashboard prerequisites and billing models, plus service-description search excerpts; no prerequisites for these planned rules were found.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics beyond the roadmap targets are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DLP auto-resolution rules; Purview DLP rule based tagging auto resolution default permissions retention resolved alerts tags. Read roadmap and cited Purview/Defender DLP alert pages; none gives rollout mechanics for the planned capability.

claims.claim: Which DLP workloads the planned rules cover is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: DLP auto-resolution rules; Purview alert tagging rules. Read roadmap and dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started: the dashboard lists workloads, but neither the record nor the documentation specifies workload coverage for the planned alert-handling rules.

claims.claim: The roadmap item describes no new data access.
claims.quote: Alert auto-resolution & tagging rules let you tell DLP, in advance, how to handle predictable alerts.

claims.claim: Existing DLP alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.
claims.quote: Alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.

claims.claim: DLP alerts can be investigated in Microsoft Defender XDR, subject to disabling its built-in DLP tuning rule as the paragraph explains.
claims.quote: When the built-in DLP alert tuning rule is disabled, you can manage and respond to Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) alerts and incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal.

claims.claim: DLP alerts can be investigated in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: DLP alerts can be investigated and managed in the Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard and in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends the Defender XDR dashboard for investigating DLP alerts.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Defender XDR dashboard is the recommended location for investigating and managing DLP alerts.

claims.claim: The documented Purview dashboard procedure tells the analyst to set Status to Resolved after taking the required action.
claims.quote: After you take the required action for the alert, set the Status of the alert to Resolved.

claims.claim: The existing Defender built-in DLP alert tuning rule took effect in early October 2026.
claims.quote: A built-in alert tuning rule for DLP signals took effect in early October 2026.

claims.claim: That built-in Defender rule sets DLP signals as behaviors instead of alerts.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Defender XDR, the rule sets these signals as behaviors instead of alerts, so they don't generate alerts or appear in the incident queue.

claims.claim: Disabling the existing built-in DLP tuning rule lets DLP signals continue to appear as alerts in Defender XDR.
claims.quote: To continue seeing DLP signals as alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR, disable the rule in Settings > Microsoft Defender XDR > Alert tuning.

claims.claim: Access to the Purview DLP alert management dashboard requires Manage alerts plus DLP Compliance Management or View-Only DLP Compliance Management.
claims.quote: To access the DLP alert management dashboard, you need the Manage alerts role and either of these two roles: DLP Compliance Management; View-Only DLP Compliance Management

claims.claim: The DLP alert management dashboard retains alerts for 30 days.
claims.quote: The DLP alert management dashboard retains alerts for 30 days.

claims.claim: Audit log retention policy configuration controls how long an alert remains visible in the console.
claims.quote: Your organization's audit log retention policy configuration controls how long an alert remains visible in the console.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The Microsoft Defender portal already supports associating custom tags with DLP incidents.
claims.quote: Associate custom tags to DLP incidents and filter by them.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether planned rule tags are the same as existing Defender custom incident tags is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview alert tagging rules; Purview DLP rule based tagging auto resolution default permissions retention resolved alerts tags. Read dlp-alert-investigation-learn and dlp-investigate-alerts-defender; they describe custom incident tags but do not connect them to the planned rule tags.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The included licensing model describes a new Purview option inside the product's published Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 per-user model for Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint assets, not a confirmed feature-specific entitlement.
claims.quote: The per-user licensing model is the familiar Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 model. It remains unchanged. This licensing model enables you to apply Microsoft Purview controls and protections to Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint-based assets.

claims.quote: Alert auto-resolution & tagging rules let you tell DLP, in advance, how to handle predictable alerts. You define a rule once, and from then on DLP applies it automatically to every new alert:

claims.claim: Single-event alert configuration is available to organisations with the DLP subscriptions listed as E1, E3, E5, F1, G1, E3, G3, E5 and G5.
claims.quote: Single-event alert configuration: All organizations with a DLP subscription (E1, E3, E5, F1, G1, E3, G3, E5, G5) can configure policies to generate an alert for every time a triggering activity occurs.

claims.claim: An A5 subscription qualifies for aggregated alert configuration.
claims.quote: Aggregated alert configuration: To configure aggregate alert policies based on a threshold, you must have either of the following configurations: An A5 subscription

claims.claim: An E5 or G5 subscription qualifies for aggregated alert configuration.
claims.quote: Aggregated alert configuration: To configure aggregate alert policies based on a threshold, you must have either of the following configurations: ... An E5 or G5 subscription

claims.claim: An E1, F1, G1, E3 or G3 subscription needs one of the documented additional features to configure aggregated alerts.
claims.quote: An E1, F1, or G1 subscription or an E3 or G3 subscription that includes one of the following features: Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection Plan 2; Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance); Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license
